title: Isolation Readiness — Workshop Synthesis and POC Checklist
content:
Purpose:
This note captures synthesis from the 2025-09-09 customer workshop (Mr. Reynolds, IT & security, and our SEs) to validate feasibility and produce a prioritized POC checklist for an isolated (air-gapped) on-prem deployment of Redwood Private. The aim is a 2-week technical POC that demonstrates restricted-network installation, model serving on local GPUs, KMS integration, and telemetry gating.

Summary (high level):
- Customer constraints: No inbound internet from deployment subnet; very limited egress via approved jump-host; strict policy for third-party binaries; Windows-based admin workstations only; RHEL 8 nodes for compute; NVIDIA A40 & A100 hardware available across two racks.
- POC goals: 1) Successful deploy of Redwood Private control plane in customer-managed vSphere cluster or bare-metal (TBD) with no internet on workload plane; 2) Serve a verified open LLM (10B float16) at 100 qps baseline; 3) Demonstrate KMS-backed key retrieval via approved HSM (PKCS#11); 4) Show labeled telemetry being written to a customer S3-compatible object store reachable only from a restricted subnet; 5) Run basic quality/regression checks using offline test harness.

Environment inventory (collected during workshop):
- Compute nodes: 6 x RHEL 8.7 servers (2x A100 40GB, 2x A40 48GB, 2x A40 24GB) — patch level and driver matrix needs confirmation.
- Orchestration: customer prefers VMware vSphere + Tanzu in 2nd phase, but for POC they can provision a flat K8s cluster (K8s 1.25) with Calico CNI.
- Storage: On-prem CEPH cluster (RGW S3-compatible) available on private subnet.
- Networking: Dedicated POC VLAN with no direct internet; jump-host (bastion) in DMZ that can pull artifacts and be pushed to internal registry via secure rsync over SFTP.
- Identity & secrets: Vault cluster (HashiCorp) reachable from K8s control plane; HSM available via PKCS#11 over isolated network segment.
- Security/compliance: Customer requires SBOM and signed container images; binary allowlist enforced; offline vulnerability scanning is done via internal tooling.

Key technical constraints and implications:
- No direct image pull from public registries: we must provide a mirroring plan (OCI tarballs + signed manifests) and an installer that can import to local registry.
- Kernel/NVIDIA driver compatibility: Drivers must be pre-approved. We need driver install instructions and a tested image matrix for RHEL 8 + NGC drivers.
- Entropy & KMS: KMS calls must go over the isolated network; fallback to local sealed key not permitted by security. We need to validate PKCS#11 flow in the POC.
- Telemetry: Outbound telemetry must be opt-in and routed to the on-prem RGW endpoint. We must demonstrate filtering to only accept token-level cost/latency metrics (no user data).
- Updates/patching: Customer disallows automatic remote updates. The installer must support offline patch bundles and manual upgrade steps.

Proposed POC approach (phased, 2 weeks):
Phase 0 — Prep (3 days):
- Confirm final node OS + driver versions; customer to provide SSH access and a node-runbook.
- Provide a mirror bundle (tar.gz) containing: container images, SBOM, helm charts, and signed manifests.
- Deliver offline installer script and import instructions for image registry (harbor) + vulnerability scan checklist.

Phase 1 — Install & Basic smoke (4 days):
- Import artifacts to local registry via rsync from jump-host.
- Run installer in dry-run, then real run with CE (control-plane) services on 3 nodes, worker pool across GPU nodes.
- Validate pods start, NVidia device plugin binds GPUs, kernel modules load.
- Smoke tests: /health endpoints, simple text generation against small model, KV cache warmup.

Phase 2 — Security integrations & telemetry (3 days):
- Configure PKCS#11 integration with customer HSM using provided test credentials; perform KMS sign/decrypt flow test.
- Configure Vault provider and secrets injector for TLS certs.
- Point telemetry agent to RGW bucket; run sample telemetry ingestion job.

Phase 3 — Load & quality checks (2 days):
- Serve verified 10B model (or smaller if memory constrained) and run a throughput/latency profile to validate target qps.
- Run offline eval suite (30 prompts) and compare output to baseline (we will provide baseline generation artifacts to customer in the mirror bundle).

Acceptance criteria (POC exit):
- Control plane and worker nodes running, with scheduler binding GPUs and model endpoints responding to local API calls.
- Model-serving throughput meets baseline (tbd numeric after inventory confirmation) and 95p latency under SLO target for test prompts.
- KMS flows demonstrate successful key retrieval/sign operations from HSM without internet.
- Telemetry uploads to RGW endpoint and contains no PII (we will provide a filtering policy).
- SBOMs and signed image manifests verified by customer scanner.

Installer & artifact requirements (deliverables from SE):
- Mirror bundle: OCI images as tarballs, Helm charts, DB migration artifacts, signed SBOM (SPDX), and signature files.
- Offline install script with clear step-by-step for image import, helm apply, and CRD creation.
- Driver compatibility matrix (RHEL kernel versions mapped to NVIDIA driver versions we tested).
- Quick troubleshooting playbook: common failure signatures and remediation commands (device plugin logs, kubelet dmesg checks, HSM pkcs11 debug).

Open questions / Risks (need customer answers before kickoff):
- Which upgrade window policies are mandatory? We need to confirm if a single-node control-plane restart is allowed.
- Can the jump-host be used to host a temporary mirror registry accessible only to the POC VLAN? If not, we must stage images on an air-gapped USB transfer (longer).
- Are there any FIPS-only crypto constraints that would prevent us from using our default TLS ciphers?
- Will the HSM team provide a test partition and PKCS#11 credentials for the POC?
- Exact performance target (qps/latency) to validate: customer mentioned "interactive latency" but did not specify numbers.

Immediate action items (owner / due):
- SE: Prepare mirror bundle (images + SBOM + signed manifests) and offline installer (Priya) — due 2025-09-15.
- Customer IT: Confirm node OS patch level & provide SSH bastion account (Reynolds) — due 2025-09-12.
- Infra SE: Run driver compatibility tests on internal lab (Evan) — due 2025-09-14.
- Security: Validate signed-image checklist and provide a short SBOM reviewer checklist (Sofia) — due 2025-09-14.

Notes / heuristics learned from session:
- Customers often prefer artifact handoff as an air-gapped tarball over running a temporary mirror in DMZ — be ready with both flows.
- Pre-validating kernel + nvidia driver combinations prevents 2-day stalls during POC.
- Keep telemetry minimal and opt-in; show clear policy for no-user-data collection.
- Provide a small test model that is guaranteed to fit in 24GB VRAM so we can validate GPU plumbing quickly before pulling heavier models.

Appendix (useful snippets to include with mirror bundle):
- Example: commands for importing OCI tar into Harbor './oras load -f images.tar'
- Example: helm install flags for offline registry override 'helm install --set image.registry=harbor.internal:5000'
- Example: pkcs11-tool command to list slots 'pkcs11-tool --list-slots --module /usr/lib/libpteidpkcs11.so'

Bottom line: POC is feasible provided customer can (A) approve a jump-host image import flow or agree to physical media transfer for images, (B) provide an HSM test partition and (C) agree to a limited offline upgrade/rollback window. Next step: confirm the three open questions with customer and lock POC start date.

-- Priya (SE)
